title: Everybody's Fine Down Here
subject: a pub on the last night before it closes
caption: Britpop, 90s UK guitar swagger. Two jangly electric guitars with chorus pedals, a driving eighth-note bass, live drums with a big open snare, tambourine doubling the backbeat. A nasal British male voice drawls the verses behind the beat and the chorus is an anthemic singalong with a whole room shouting the second half. Raw live-room bleed, tape saturation, no vocal tuning. 128 BPM, A major. Cocky, warm, a bit sad underneath.
lyrics:
[Intro - Guitars]

[Verse 1]
They're selling off the optics Sunday
The dartboard's going to Dave
Forty years of somebody's grandad
In the carpet, in the wallpaper

[Pre-Chorus]
Last orders means it this time

[Chorus]
Everybody's fine down here
Everybody's absolutely fine
We'll drink the place completely dry
And pretend we've all got somewhere else to go

[Verse 2]
The landlord's crying in the cellar
He thinks that nobody knows
We all know, we just let him
It's the decent thing to do

[Guitar Solo]

[Chorus]
Everybody's fine down here
Everybody's absolutely fine
We'll drink the place completely dry
And pretend we've all got somewhere else to go

[Outro - crowd]
Fine down here
Fine down here
